newsitem.title: CROATIA: Serbs assault Croatian officials in rebel enclave.
newsitem.headline: Serbs assault Croatian officials in rebel enclave.

text.p: A group of Serbs assaulted Croatian officials handing out pensions in Croatia's last Serb-held enclave on Tuesday, stoning their bus and smashing windows in their office, a U.N. spokesman said.

"A group of young men this morning threw rocks at the Croatian mobile pension payment office in Borovo Selo," Yuri Chizik, deputy spokesman of the U.N. Transitional Authority for Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES), told Reuters.
He said they broke the glass door of the office and stoned the bus of the Croatian officials, which was parked nearby. Nobody was injured in the incident.

There are several permanent and mobile pension payment offices in the region, manned by Croatian officials. They are now handing out pensions for the first time in five years, in a government attempt to improve relations with its Serb minority.
Croatian officials were escorted from the pension payment office by Russian UNTAES soldiers and transported to Croatian territory, Chizik said.
Eastern Slavonia saw some of the worst fighting during the minority Serb rebellion against Croatia's bid for independence from federal Yugoslavia in 1991.

The area is now under control of UNTAES, with 5,000 troops, but will revert to Croatian rule by mid-1997. Croatia recaptured other Serb-held enclaves in two surprise offensives in 1995, which led to an exodus of the Serb population.
Another Croatian bus was stoned by local Serbs last weekend, UNTAES officials said.

Many Serbs in the enclave remain hostile to Croatian authority and have protested against the gradual reinstatement of Croatian institutions or UNTAES-assisted visits by Croat refugees preparing to resettle in their homes.
A bomb exploded outside a Catholic church in the region earlier this month. Serbs also attacked Croat refugees attending a Christmas Eve mass, injuring a U.N. worker.
